questions.q: What checkpoint does four-way matching add on top of three-way matching?
options: A second receipt from a different warehouse
Inspection and acceptance of the received goods
A duplicate purchase order
An approval from the supplier's own finance team
questions.explain: Four-way matching adds inspection/acceptance -- confirming the goods not only arrived but met the PO's quality requirements.

questions.q: Why do most organizations limit four-way matching to only certain purchase orders?
options: Because it is required by law for every PO
Because it replaces the need for a purchase order entirely
Because it adds real process time, so it's reserved for high-value or high-risk purchases
Because it is only available for service purchase orders
questions.explain: The extra inspection step is valuable but costs time, so it's typically applied selectively rather than universally.

questions.q: In the Meridian Office Supply example, 50 chairs are received but only 47 are accepted after inspection. What happens to an invoice for 50 chairs?
options: It is placed on hold because invoiced quantity exceeds accepted quantity
It validates immediately because all 50 were received
It is automatically corrected to 47 units with no hold
The supplier is blocked from invoicing again
questions.explain: Four-way matching checks against accepted quantity, not just received quantity, so the invoice holds until resolved.

questions.q: What is a tolerance set used for?
options: Defining how many approval levels an invoice requires
Determining which ledger an invoice posts to
Setting the supplier's payment terms
Bundling the percentage/amount limits that decide when a PO-to-invoice variance creates a hold
questions.explain: A tolerance set groups quantity and price tolerances together and is assigned at the supplier, site, or category level.

questions.q: Why does each exceeded tolerance create its own distinctly named hold (e.g., Price hold vs. Quantity Received hold)?
options: So the invoice can never be paid
So whoever resolves the hold knows exactly which mismatch to address
Because Oracle requires a unique hold name for every invoice
Because each hold type uses a different currency
questions.explain: Named holds point directly at the specific variance causing the problem, speeding up resolution.
